extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unleaming for LLMs
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset and evaluation task for machine unlearning in large language models, consisting of synthetic fictitious author biographies with question-answer pairs and associated forget/retain splits.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated by prompting GPT-4 to generate biographies for completely fictitious fictitious authors using seeded attributes such as birthplace, gender, year of birth, genre, awards, parents, and book titles, and then generating 20 question-answer pairs for each author. The paper also states that book-title keywords were seeded using the Goodreads Books dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetic author biographies and question-answer pairs generated by GPT-4; book-title keywords seeded from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors modified the prompting strategy to deterministically seed author attributes and reduce repeated/bias-prone words in the generated text; they also created forget and retain splits from the synthetic dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The raw synthetic dataset was refined by using a more elaborate prompt to improve diversity and by manually inspecting the generated data for diversity; the final benchmark includes 90-10, 95-5, and 99-1 retain/forget splits.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol is described. The dataset was generated by GPT-4, which produced the biographies and question-answer pairs, and GPT-4 was also used to paraphrase answers and generate factually incorrect perturbations for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: GPT-4 was used to paraphrase answers and generate five perturbed incorrect answers for the Truth Ratio metric; the paper uses a KS-test to compare Truth Ratio distributions between retain and unleamed models.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 20 question-answer pairs per fictitious author; five perturbed answers were generated per question for the Truth Ratio evaluation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark is designed around fictitious author profiles with attributes including birthplace, gender, year of birth, genre, awards, and parents' professions; these are synthetic and not real people.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by privacy and the Right to be Forgotten for large language models, aiming to help evaluate methods that remove sensitive or private information from trained models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly notes that initial prompting caused repeated words and strong biases in generated biographies, such as overuse of certain terms and concentrated birth years; it also states that seeding attributes was used to reduce leakage of pretraining biases into the synthetic data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only covers entity-level forgetting of information learned during finetuning, not pretraining; it does not address instance-level or behavior-level unlearning, in-context unlearning, or finding forget/retain sets in real-world settings. The paper also notes that its forget-quality metric is only an approximation of indistinguishability and that models producing gibberish can appear to have strong forget quality.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of machine unlearning methods for LLMs; finetuning on the synthetic dataset; testing forget quality and model utility on forget set, retain set, real authors, and world facts.
